question: Should OpenClaw intentionally make configured jq safeBins fail closed in this PR, even though existing approval-free jq safe-bin workflows will require allowlist entries or prompts after upgrade?
rationale: The patch tightens an approval-free exec boundary, but it changes a documented/configured operator workflow, so automation should not decide the security-versus-compatibility policy alone.

options.title: Accept fail-closed jq
options.body: Merge this direction after maintainer acceptance because jq cannot be proven to stay within the stdin-only safe-bin model and the PR preserves explicit allowlist and prompt paths.

options.title: Preserve jq compatibility
options.body: Require the branch to keep simple jq filters approval-free and pursue narrower parser-backed hardening, accepting that jq modules/startup behavior remains hard to constrain.

options.title: Add opt-in strict policy
options.body: Keep shipped jq safeBins behavior compatible by default and add a separate strict policy surface, at the cost of new configuration and product complexity.

recommendation.title: Accept fail-closed jq
recommendation.body: Merge this direction after maintainer acceptance because jq cannot be proven to stay within the stdin-only safe-bin model and the PR preserves explicit allowlist and prompt paths.

likelyOwner.reason: Vincent Koc is the strongest recent current-main history signal for both the safe-bin semantic code and the prior fail-closed broad-tool pattern.
